newsitem.title: INDIA: India, U.S officials hold technical talks on wheat.
newsitem.headline: India, U.S officials hold technical talks on wheat.

text.p: A U.S. delegation held talks on Thursday with senior Indian government officials on technical issues concerning wheat, officials said.

"Technical points on wheat were discussed during talks between the visiting U.S. team and Food Secretary S.P. Jakhanwal," a Food Ministry spokesperson told Reuters. She did not give details of the meeting.
The U.S. team also met Agriculture Secretary K. Rajan but details of the meeting were not known. Officials of the delegation could not be reached for comment.
Later on Thursday, the U.S. team exchanged views with officials of state-run State Trading Corp (STC), led by its chairman B.K. Chaturvedi.
The Indian government, after a fall in stocks, authorised STC in December 1996 to import wheat to augment supplies and stabilise domestic prices.
STC officials said earlier this month that it had contracted to import 2.74 million tonnes since December, mostly from Australia, Canada and Argentina.
The Times of India newspaper on Thursday quoted Food Ministry officials as saying the the United States was upset at not being able to sell any wheat to India so far.
"We understand that the U.S. side is quite upset at losing contracts," the newspaper quoted a ministry official as saying.
"But that cannot be helped because on an average the prices offered by the U.S. suppliers are $15-20 per tonne higher than the prices offered by suppliers from, say, Australia."
A U.S. embassy spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday the U. S. delegation would hold talks with Indian officials on on wheat specifications, but the talks would not cover sales to India.
"There will be no negotiations on wheat contracts," the spokesman said.

The team, which is visiting India, includes representatives of the U.S. Department of Agriculture and U.S. Wheat Associates, plus two members of private companies with extensive expertise in contract procedures.
U.S. Wheat Associates is a non-profit association representing wheat farmers and provides technical assistance to consumers.
